title: Applied labs
description: Build, break, debug and evaluate in your own environment.

lessons.title: Lab: Architecture & durable execution
lessons.conceptOverview: Model a research assistant as a state machine. Crash immediately after a tool succeeds but before state is saved; design recovery without duplicating the action.
lessons.whyItMatters: Build durable, observable agents with bounded authority.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Use a fixed workflow when the steps are known. Routers select handlers; planner-executor and supervisor architectures allocate work dynamically. Long-running agents require durable state, checkpoints and explicit transitions. External side effects need idempotency keys or reconciliation because retries can repeat actions.

sections.title: 1. Establish a baseline
sections.content: Write down your inputs, expected behavior and constraints before starting. Model a research assistant as a state machine. Crash immediately after a tool succeeds but before state is saved; design recovery without duplicating the action.

sections.title: 2. Introduce a failure
sections.content: Test the mistaken assumption: Retrying every failed step is safe for external side effects. Record the observed result and the point where it diverges from your prediction.

sections.title: 3. Debug and evaluate
sections.content: Use the mechanism to explain the failure: Use a fixed workflow when the steps are known. Routers select handlers; planner-executor and supervisor architectures allocate work dynamically. Long-running agents require durable state, checkpoints and explicit transitions. External side effects need idempotency keys or reconciliation because retries can repeat actions. Change one variable at a time. Repeat the baseline and add a held-out case. Submit the implementation, results and limitations.

commonMistakes: Retrying every failed step is safe for external side effects.
keyTakeaways: Use a fixed workflow when the steps are known.

lessons.title: Lab: Computer use & memory
lessons.conceptOverview: Design an observe-act-verify loop for a browser form. Define stale-state detection, action limits and which actions require explicit user authorization.
lessons.whyItMatters: Build durable, observable agents with bounded authority.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: A computer-use agent observes an environment, chooses an action and verifies the resulting state. UI text is untrusted input. Episodic memory records events, semantic memory stores facts and procedural memory captures reusable methods. Retrieval and consolidation need provenance, expiration and correction policies.

lessons.title: Lab: Trajectory evaluation
lessons.conceptOverview: Create ten scenarios including tool timeouts, poisoned content and ambiguous instructions. Score completion and authorization violations separately.
lessons.whyItMatters: Build durable, observable agents with bounded authority.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Task completion alone can hide unsafe or expensive trajectories. Measure tool selection and argument accuracy, policy violations, recovery rate, cost and latency. Evaluate repeat runs because stochastic agents can vary. Report failures by step and maintain adversarial cases alongside normal tasks.
